summary: Gadjin Nagao was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, later serving on its faculty from 1935 to 1971 as Chair of Buddhist Studies.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gananath Obeyesekere worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of Washington, and held teaching posts at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He headed the department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held posts at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Calcutta.

Ganganatha Jha worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, and Allahabad. He served as professor at Muir Central College, principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and vice chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).
Gangzhun is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and Northwest Minzu University under MA supervisor Alak Dorje Rinpoche.
Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik and with traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Jean Daniel Kieffer. He held the chair of Indian languages at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (1828–1878).

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar, later teaching Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (1979–1994), Columbia University (1999–2007), and the University of Chicago (2007–2021).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, and served as Associate Director at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).
Gary Goh Wee Kian is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hui-Chieh Loy, Jay L. Garfield, Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley, trained under several Buddhist teachers, and served as a professor at the University of California, Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton is a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, University of New Mexico, and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held faculty posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair of Sanskrit at the University of Turin (1852) and served as director of the National University Library of Turin (1859).

Gaston Paris was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1869–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the École Polytechnique from roughly 1898 to 1900.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
